comparison_intro: One behavior contract, three implementations. Run the companion files and the same three acceptance tests against shared fixture data.

language_notes.sas: SAS LENGTH ignores trailing ordinary blanks and returns 1 for an all-blank character value; LENGTH is byte-based.
language_notes.python: Pad stored text to 10. Remove only ordinary trailing spaces for len, then enforce a minimum of 1; keep stored text intact.
language_notes.r: The base R pattern " +$" removes trailing ordinary spaces only. nchar counts the remaining ASCII characters; pmax enforces 1.

semantic_notes.title: Trailing spaces only
semantic_notes.text: Leading spaces and tabs remain meaningful. Broad whitespace trimming changes the rule even if the original numeric results happen to match.

semantic_notes.title: Length differs from width
semantic_notes.text: Every stored value has width 10. LENGTH counts through the final nonblank character and returns 1 for the all-blank value.

tests.name: Original five-row fixture
tests.input: ABC, ABC, ABCDEFGHIJ, X and character missing decoded as an empty string.
tests.expected: len = [3, 3, 10, 1, 1]; every stored text value is padded to width 10.
tests.catches: Counting storage padding, losing character-missing blanks, or returning zero for an all-blank value.

tests.name: Added meaningful-space boundary
tests.input: Added validation strings " ABC  ", "ABC<tab>" and three spaces; CSV contains the actual tab.
tests.expected: len = [4, 4, 1]; leading space and tab survive; all-blank result is 1.
tests.catches: strip() removing leading blanks, broad whitespace rstrip(), or omitting the minimum of 1.

tests.name: Preservation, widths and order
tests.input: All shared rows reversed; original caller data saved.
tests.expected: Caller unchanged; returned text equals expected padded text; integer lengths and row order retained.
tests.catches: Mutating or trimming stored text, losing padding, wrong result type or row reordering.

scope: Single-byte ASCII text up to width 10, including ordinary spaces and tab. Character missing is a blank string. No Unicode byte/character equivalence or numeric-argument coercion claim.
